goal: Implement the first runtime Evaluation module for an already-submitted TrainingAttempt. Judge the user's analysis process using only the attempt's submission-time knowledge boundary, produce the frozen shared Evaluation contract with at most one primary error and two contributors, support justified abstention, and return diagnostic feedback without LearningState or Review mutation.
acceptance: Consume an already-submitted canonical published TrainingAttempt. The user's initial analysis is authoritative input and must never be generated, overwritten, revised, or mutated by Evaluation.

Judge the reasoning and observations captured at submission, never subsequent market movement. Do not reward lucky predictions, penalize a sound process because of later outcomes, or predict future price action.

Use only attempt.context.knowledge_boundary frozen at submission for formal positive or negative judgment. Later Learning Map changes and later learned concepts must not retroactively change Evaluation authority.

Derive formal Error ID eligibility internally from the canonical S1-S3 Learning Map Error-to-Concept and Error-to-Skill mappings plus the immutable TrainingAttempt boundary. Each formal primary or contributor error requires a supporting mapped Concept ID that was CORE, permitted by the attempt's Stage, and learned at submission. Reject forged or expanded caller-supplied boundaries.

Use only the 19 approved S1-S3 Error IDs: OBS-001, OBS-002, OBS-004, STR-001, STR-002, STR-006, STR-007, STR-003, STR-004, STR-005, REA-002, REA-003, REA-005, LOC-001, LOC-002, LOC-003, LOC-004, LOC-005, and LOC-006. S1 attempts cannot receive S2/S3 formal errors; S2 attempts cannot receive S3 formal errors. No S4-S8 judgment is authorized.

Keep judgment relevant to the attempt's observation_task, primary_objective, target_concept_id, Stage, and submission-time knowledge boundary; do not expand one attempt into an unrestricted whole-chart review.

Return exactly the shared Evaluation fields attempt_id, what_was_correct, primary_issue, primary_error, contributors, hint, skill_signal, evaluation_confidence, and abstain. Do not modify docs/CONTRACTS.md or add persistent shared Evaluation fields or a parallel record.
Allow at most one primary_error, including no primary_error for a correct analysis or an abstention. Reject attempts to encode multiple primary errors in another field.

Allow zero, one, or two contributors only. The Evaluation spec must choose the smallest immutable representation inside the existing contributors field; contributors cannot bypass the single-primary-error limit or become an unlimited issue list.

Support abstain for insufficient information, genuinely ambiguous evidence, low Evaluation confidence, or a proposed formal criticism dependent on knowledge not learned at submission. When abstain is true, emit no formal primary_error and no manufactured contributor errors. A correct analysis without a detected error is not automatically an abstention.
Preserve useful correct observations in what_was_correct. Formal positive assessment must also fit the attempt's historical CORE, Stage, and learned-knowledge boundary.
Keep primary_issue and hint diagnostic and educational. A hint must not function as a second primary error, S4-S8 judgment, trading signal, or market forecast.

Bind skill_signal to one existing Learning Map skill consistent with the attempt's Stage and any eligible formal error mapping: SKL-S1-MARKET-STATE, SKL-S2-STRUCTURE-MOVEMENT, or SKL-S3-MARKET-LOCATION. Create no new skills or LearningState transition.

Define the smallest representation of evaluation_confidence needed for evaluator certainty and abstention, separate from Learning Map Knowledge Confidence; do not create a score, ranking, or reward engine.

The MVP may construct a validated Evaluation from a canonical TrainingAttempt and structured diagnostic content supplied by an evaluator/GPT caller. It owns the Evaluation contract and judgment-boundary enforcement, not LLM transport, prompt infrastructure, market-data retrieval, persistence, or network access.

Review every public Evaluation constructor and factory against caller-owned mutable collections and nested aliases, duck-typed and equality-spoofed objects, forged TrainingAttempt/context/boundary objects, invalid Stage/Error/Skill combinations, duplicate primary/contributor misuse, future-stage or unlearned-concept errors, later-learning contamination, invalid abstain combinations, malformed evaluation_confidence, and mapping-bypass attempts. Store immutable canonical content without retaining mutable caller-owned objects.

Normally materialize only spec/evaluation/EVALUATION_SPEC.md, src/price_action_learning/evaluation/__init__.py, src/price_action_learning/evaluation/core.py, and tests/evaluation/test_evaluation.py; remove spec/evaluation/.gitkeep only if present. Freeze exact business file mutations in the later governed execution instruction after live verification. Create no placeholders, shared utils/helpers/common modules, or new top-level directories.

Evaluation tests must cover canonical TrainingAttempt acceptance, preservation of user analysis, a correct-analysis path without primary error, exactly one primary error, rejection of more than one, zero/one/two contributors, rejection of more than two, abstain with no formal error, and non-abstaining correct analysis.

Evaluation tests must cover S1 rejection of S2/S3 formal errors, S2 rejection of S3 formal errors, rejection of an unlearned supporting concept, eligibility of an allowed learned CORE supporting concept, and unchanged authority after later learning or Learning Map changes.

Evaluation tests must cover Error-to-Skill consistency, target/objective/observation-task relevance, independence from future market outcomes, immutable output, hostile direct constructors, caller mutation isolation, and duck-typed or equality-spoofed input rejection or safe canonicalization.
All existing Training tests and the full project test suite must pass before future implementation completion.
Do not mutate LearningState, schedule Review, implement Study Entry or revision workflow, rewrite TrainingAttempt, change Learning Map concepts/errors/skills, or implement S4-S8.

Do not implement scoring, ranking, gamification, rewards, market prediction, trading signals, indicators, automatic trading, screenshot interpretation, TradingView API, database/persistence, API server, Web UI, plugin, generalized validation framework, or a shared abstraction for anticipated reuse.
